interface.title: Plottle (v2.0.1), a Streamlit GUI for scientific data visualization and analysis
interface.field: General physical and chemical sciences: kinetics, spectroscopy (IR/Raman, NMR, UV-Vis, mass spec), lab measurements
interface.stage_of_work: Data exploration, analysis and figure making after data has been collected
interface.what_it_is_for: Load tabular or spectral data, look it over, plot it, run fits, statistics and peak analysis on one dataset or several, and export figures, tables and reports.

data.note: Uploaded experimental_data.csv (20 rows × 4 columns: Temperature, Pressure, Volume, Sample). Loaded two built-in examples from Data Upload > Example Datasets: reaction_kinetics.csv (120 × 4) and ir_spectrum.csv (1801 × 2; wavenumber_cm-1 descending from about 4000, and transmittance). Typing a page's URL into the address bar started a new session and wiped the loaded datasets (screens/032.webp). Navigation after that used only the sidebar, and the two examples were loaded again.

features.name: File upload with instant preview and summary statistics
features.general: Drop in a data file and right away see its size, the first and last rows, column types and per-column summary statistics, then switch between loaded datasets.
features.specific: Data Upload > Upload File: the uploader accepts CSV, XLSX, TSV, JSON, Parquet, JDX, HDF5, mzML and more. It shows the shape, a head/tail preview grid, a Quick Statistics expander (count, mean, std, quartiles) and a Loaded Datasets picker with rows, columns, memory and column types. A Delete button is present but was not pressed.
steps: Pick a file in the uploader
Read the shape and the preview rows
Expand Quick Statistics
Choose a dataset in Loaded Datasets to see its column types
serves_tasks: Load a table from a local file and see its shape, contents and summary statistics

features.name: Example dataset gallery cards
features.general: A grid of cards for bundled sample datasets. Each card describes the data, names the plot types it suits and has a Load button that adds it to the session. Loaded data lives in the browser session and is lost if the session restarts.
features.specific: Example Datasets tab: Normal/Bimodal Distribution, Sine & Cosine, Scatter Correlation, Grouped Categorical, Molecular Properties, IR Spectrum, Reaction Kinetics, Gaussian Surface and Correlation Matrix, each with 'Best for:' hints and a Load button. Opening a page by typing its URL starts a new session and drops loaded datasets; use the sidebar.
steps: Open the Example Datasets tab
Read a card's description and 'Best for' hints
Press Load
Use the dataset in any plot or analysis page, reached through the sidebar
serves_tasks: Load bundled example datasets instead of your own files

features.name: Quick plot builder with style and labels
features.general: Pick a dataset, a plotting library and a plot type, map columns to the axes, set style and labels, and generate the figure. Zoom, annotation and export panels sit below the plot; in this run the annotation did not change the plot and the PNG export produced no file, and zoom was not opened.
features.specific: Quick Plot: dataset, library (Matplotlib) and plot type (Scatter Plot) pickers; X and Y column; color, point size and opacity; width and height; title and axis labels; Generate Plot (adds to plot history). Below the plot: Convert to Plotly and Zoom / Axis Range (not tried), Annotations (horizontal line at y=1 had no visible effect) and Export plot & data (PNG 150/300/600 dpi, SVG, PDF, CSV listed; PNG 300 dpi gave no file).
steps: Choose a dataset, library and plot type
Choose the X and Y columns and set the style
Type a title and axis labels
Press Generate Plot
serves_tasks: Make a titled scatter plot of two variables

features.name: Curve fit with model choice, parameters, R² and overlay plot
features.general: Choose x and y variables and a model family, run the fit, and read the fitted parameters, goodness of fit and equation, with the fitted curve drawn over the data. Check the overlay: a nonlinear model run without starting values can converge to a degenerate solution.
features.specific: Analysis Tools > Curve Fitting: X and Y variable, Fit type (Linear, Polynomial, Exponential, Custom), 'Show fitted curve plot' checkbox, Run Fit. Results show the parameters (slope/intercept, or a, b, c), R² with a quality label, the equation and a Data vs Fit plot, saved to analysis history. On reaction_kinetics the built-in Exponential collapsed to a straight line (b≈2.5e-6, R² 0.747, same as Linear). Custom was seen but not run.
steps: Choose the X and Y variables
Choose a fit type
Press Run Fit
Read the parameters, R² and equation
Check the overlay plot for a degenerate fit before trusting the parameters
serves_tasks: Fit straight-line and exponential models to a decay curve and read their parameters and goodness of fit (the exponential fit, run without starting values, collapsed to a straight line)

features.name: Threshold-based peak finder with interactive peak plot and peak report
features.general: Set height, distance, prominence and width thresholds, detect maxima in a 1-D signal, see them marked on a zoomable plot and get a table of position, height, prominence, width and area. It finds maxima only, so absorption dips in a transmittance trace are missed, and widths and areas come out negative when the x-axis runs high to low.
features.specific: Peak Fitting > Find & Measure: X and Y column, Min height, Min distance, Min prominence, Min width, Find Peaks. Shows a Plotly 'Detected Peaks' chart with numbered markers, a Peak Report table (Position, Height, Prominence, FWHM, Area) and 'Download peak report (CSV)'. On ir_spectrum transmittance with default thresholds: 253 noise maxima, negative FWHM and Area. A Fit Peaks sub-tab was seen but not opened.
steps: Choose the X and Y columns
Set the detection thresholds
Press Find Peaks
Look at the marked peaks on the interactive plot
Read the Peak Report, checking signs of FWHM and Area
serves_tasks: Run a threshold peak finder on a spectrum with default settings (on a transmittance trace it marked noise maxima, not the absorption dips, and every width and area came out negative)

features.name: IR band-assignment lookup
features.general: For a spectrum, choose the axis and intensity columns, set a minimum intensity for peaks, and get a table of peak positions with candidate band assignments from a rule table. The intensity is read as absorbance; a transmittance trace gave noise points with no assignments.
features.specific: Spectroscopy > IR / Raman > Operation 'Band Assignment': Wavenumber and Absorbance/Intensity columns, 'Min absorbance for peaks', Assign Bands, table of Wavenumber, Absorbance, Possible Assignments. Seen on the same panel but not run: Absorbance ↔ Transmittance, ATR Correction, Spectral Subtraction, Remove Cosmic Rays, the NIST WebBook Lookup expander, and the NMR, UV-Vis and Mass Spec tabs.
steps: Choose the source dataset
Choose the wavenumber and intensity columns
Choose Band Assignment and set the minimum absorbance
Press Assign Bands and read the table
serves_tasks: Run a rule-table lookup of band assignments on a spectrum (with transmittance read as absorbance, it listed noise points and no assignments)

features.name: Batch statistics across datasets with downloadable summary
features.general: Pick several loaded datasets and compute summary statistics for all their columns in one run. The results come back as one long table (dataset × column × statistic) that you can download.
features.specific: Analyze > Batch > Statistics: dataset multiselect, Run Statistics, a results table (n, mean, median, std, min, max, q1, q3, iqr), Download CSV (batch_statistics.csv). The table disappears from the page after the download. Curve Fit and Peak Analysis sub-tabs and a Workflow Presets tab were seen but not run.
steps: Select the datasets
Open the Statistics tab
Press Run Statistics
Read the combined table
Download the combined CSV
serves_tasks: Compute summary statistics for every column of several datasets and download the table
